sections.html:
Chesapeake is an independent city in Hampton Roads, in southeastern Virginia. Portsmouth and Norfolk lie to its north, Virginia Beach to the east, Suffolk to the west, and North Carolina's Currituck and Camden counties to the south. The 2020 census counted 249,422 residents, and the city holds about 338.5 square miles of land plus 12.4 of water.

Six boroughs make up the city: South Norfolk, Butts Road, Deep Creek, Pleasant Grove, Western Branch and Washington. A house in one can feel nothing like a house in another, from tight older streets to big rural lots.

Average elevation is only 16 feet, and water is everywhere, so ask the city for the flood zone of your parcel before you list, especially if the lot is near water.

Most Virginia localities bill twice a year. Chesapeake bills four times. The Treasurer's due dates page sets the schedule below, and a date on a weekend or holiday shifts to the next business day.

PaymentDue date
1st quarterSeptember 30
2nd quarterDecember 31
3rd quarterMarch 31
4th quarterJune 5
Stormwater, 1st halfJune 5
Stormwater, 2nd halfDecember 31
Tax relief filingBy May 15

A payment that is neither postmarked nor received by its deadline picks up penalty and interest as state and city code require. Ask the Treasurer for the exact percentages. State law in Code of Virginia 58.1-3916 caps the property tax penalty at 10 percent and interest at 10 percent a year.

sections.h2: The tax rate and the stormwater fee
sections.html:
For fiscal year 2026 to 2027 the city lists a real estate rate of $1.01 per $100 of assessed value, and $0.01 of that goes to mosquito control. A single residence pays a stormwater fee of $136.20 a year, split into two installments of $68.10.

City Code Section 26-372 makes the stormwater fee payable by the owner of the billed parcel. If that bill is unpaid when you list, it can still be sitting there at closing.

To reach the Treasurer, email paytax@cityofchesapeake.net or call the city main line at 757-382-2489. The office is at 306 Cedar Road, Chesapeake, VA 23322.

sections.h2: How the Assessor sets and changes values
sections.html:
Values are set as of January 1 and take effect July 1. Owners whose value changed are mailed a notice, and for the current cycle that happens on or before March 1, 2027.

New construction, additions and demolitions arrive through supplemental bills, with value changes picked up on October 1, January 1, April 1 and July 1. That means a teardown or an addition finished before you list can change the bill partway through the year.

The Assessor is on the 4th Floor at 306 Cedar Road. Call 757-382-6235 or email assessor@cityofchesapeake.net. A free property search is available at chesapeake.civ.quest.

Owners have three routes and may use more than one. You can ask the Assessor to schedule a property review, apply to the Board of Equalization, or petition the Circuit Court.

  • A Board application has to show the property is valued above fair market value, that the assessment is applied unevenly, or that it ignores accepted appraisal standards or Virginia law.
  • The city posts an Appeal Process guide, filing instructions and an application as PDFs.
  • Time limits apply. Ask the Assessor's office for them before you plan.

sections.h2: Relief for owners over 65 or disabled
sections.html: The Commissioner of the Revenue runs tax relief, reachable at 757-382-6455, option 4. Applications are taken from January 1 through May 15. In fiscal year 2025 the city listed relief of 100 percent for household income up to $25,000. Limits are posted by year, so check the current ones before you count on a figure.

sections.h2: What the climate means for the house
sections.html: With hot, humid summers, a crawl space or attic with weak ventilation is the usual trouble spot, and a buyer's inspector will look at moisture first. Fix leaks and vents before you list, because a house with deferred upkeep shows those problems fast.

Before closing, confirm four items: the current quarter's real estate tax, the stormwater fee, any land use enrollment and the recordation costs. The city notes that Virginia does not allow a title to transfer when delinquent taxes are paid through a tax lien sale, so leaving back taxes alone can complicate a sale.

For land in the use value program, the minimums are 5 acres for agricultural, horticultural and open space land and 20 acres for forest land. A change in use or a rezoning at the owner's request can trigger rollback taxes covering the current year and the five most recent complete tax years, plus simple interest.

The state grantor tax on the deed is fifty cents per $500 of value under 58.1-802. Cash Home Buyers can buy a Chesapeake house in its present condition, even one with overdue tax, and the Treasurer's payoff can be paid from the proceeds.

sections.h2: Why four payments change the picture for a seller
sections.html:
With bills coming every three months, a closing almost always lands near a due date. A house sold in late March has the third-quarter bill just paid or about to be due, and one sold in early June meets the fourth-quarter and first stormwater dates in the same week. Ask the Treasurer which quarters show as paid, and have the closing agent split the open quarter by contract.

Owners who inherit a Chesapeake house should look at the stormwater fee too. It is billed separately from the real estate tax, so a seller can clear one and still owe the other. Request both balances in writing and keep the receipts with the closing file. If a supplemental bill follows a teardown or addition, add that to the list before the closing date.

sections.h2: What to bring when you call an office
sections.html: Have the parcel address ready, along with your latest assessment notice and the last tax bill. The Treasurer's office handles payments and payoffs, the Assessor handles values and property reviews, and the Commissioner of the Revenue handles relief for older and disabled owners. Calling the right office first saves a transfer and a second call. Ask each one to confirm any date or amount by email so you have it in writing. Dates that move for weekends or holidays are easy to miss, so write down the adjusted day and not only the one on the schedule.

1. Find out which quarterly bills you have paid and which are still ahead.
  2. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff that matches your closing date.
  3. Check the stormwater fee and confirm which installment is open.
  4. Look at your flood zone and have the paperwork ready for buyers.
  5. Ask the Assessor whether any teardown, addition or other work is waiting to be picked up on a supplemental bill.

faqs.q: When are Chesapeake real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Four payments a year: September 30, December 31, March 31 and June 5. A date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the Chesapeake real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The city lists $1.01 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2026 to 2027, with $0.01 of it for mosquito control.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Chesapeake assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Real Estate Assessor at 757-382-6235 to set up a property review, apply to the Board of Equalization, or petition the Circuit Court. You may use more than one route.

faqs.q: What is the Chesapeake stormwater fee?
faqs.a: $136.20 a year for a single residence, paid in two installments of $68.10 on June 5 and December 31. The owner of the billed parcel pays it.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Chesapeake house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, the balance is normally settled from the proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff that matches your closing date.
